correctness.rationale: From the exact SWAP-measurement adjoint identity, the star pair generator is the incidence block diag(aI,I) with off-diagonal -C/2. Since CC^T=(m-2)I+11^T, the singular-value sectors give the complete spectrum including \(m=2\) and \(n=2\) boundaries. Irreducible symmetric M-matrix Perron–Frobenius forces the minimal eigenvalue into the positive, leaf-symmetric constant block; its trace and determinant give the displayed gap for \(0<\lambda\le1\). Rationalization and the all-ones Rayleigh quotient yield asymptotic absorber-bound saturation. Comparing to the published cycle rate reduces to \(p_n(z_n)=1-(n+2)(1-\cos(\pi/n))+4(1-\cos(\pi/n))^2\): exact signs at \(n=3,4,5\),6 and cos bound for \(n\ge7\) prove the sharp crossover. Direct Kraus-operator matrices agree with the pair generator at \(n=3,4,5\) and multiple strengths; full spectrum and crossover finite checks passed. Finite tests do not replace the analytic proof. This is a pair-sector claim, not an asserted exact full-Liouvillian gap.

originality.rationale: Two closely related primary full texts were inspected. The November 2026 paper supplies all-graph operator closure, ring spectra, universal absorber throughput, and all-to-all solution, but its listed graph-specific solutions and searchable sections do not give the measured star incidence spectrum or exact topology crossover. The October 2025 precursor gives the general transport mapping and regular geometry scaling. Actual semantic index and literature queries for the star-specific spectrum and aliases found no decisive covering statement. These observations support, but cannot prove, publication priority. The generic closure, standard incidence singular values, and known cycle eigenvalues are explicitly credited.
residual_risks: The new spectral calculation is a graph-specific consequence of a previously established general generator; independently published equivalent star specializations might be overlooked or unindexed.
Classical incidence-matrix eigenvalues are known; no combinatorial originality is claimed for them alone.

value.rationale: The measurement graph is a natural design variable in quantum feedback preparation. The result identifies an edge-minimal connected topology whose pair-relaxation rate attains the universal \(O(n^{-1})\) absorber throughput asymptotically, while the standard periodic nearest-neighbor chain remains \(O(n^{-2})\). The complete star spectrum and sharp finite crossover at \(n=6\) quantify the gain and clarify exactly which measurement-resource normalization enables it. This offers a structural network-design benchmark and a precise caveat for practical per-vertex constraints, not a tiny numerical refinement or arbitrary finite instance.
